IT 505 · Fundamentals of Database Technologies · lab environment, guide 3 of 4

Guide 3 · The database toolbox

One script installs and configures every program that the class demonstrations and the three labs use: flat and file-based databases, a relational server, non-relational stores, big-data tools, the base of a blockchain, and the notebook that reads from all of them. Then you prove that each one works.

about 40 minutes, most of it waiting5 database families8 animations18 actions1 script: it505_setup.sh
How to use this guide. Work from top to bottom and tick each action when it is done; the page remembers your ticks on this computer. Each animation starts by itself, can be paused and stepped through one instruction at a time, and can be saved as a GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) picture file with its Download button. The menu stays at the top while you scroll; every section can be folded with its own button or with the floating button at the bottom right. In the dark boxes, a line that begins with # or -- explains the command below it; the Copy button of a terminal box copies the command without that line.
This guide is a Cyber.SoHo educational material. Its use is governed by the Legal Notice, Terms of Use and Acceptable Use Policy of Cyber.SoHo. You install software on your own equipment on your own responsibility; check every download as described in the guide. Details are in the section Legal at the end.
Start

Five families, one toolbox

What is installed, under which licence, and where the course uses it
Why this step. The course compares five families of databases. Having all of them on one machine lets you put the same data into each and see the differences yourself.
ToolVersion on 21 November 2026LicenceFamily and use in the course
PostgreSQL18.7; role it505, database mercadilloPostgreSQL LicenseRelational: Classes 4 to 10, Labs 1 and 2. Its JSONB (binary JSON, a data type of PostgreSQL) type also serves the document family in Class 11.
DBeaver Community26.2.5 (15 November 2026)Apache 2.0The graphical client for PostgreSQL, DuckDB and SQLite, from Class 1.
SQLite3.46 (Debian's package)Public domainFile-based: Class 2.
DuckDB2.0.1, command line and PythonMIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the origin of the licence of that name)File-based and analytical: Classes 2 and 12; reads CSV (Comma-Separated Values), JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) and Parquet files directly.
JupyterLab with pandas, SQLAlchemy, psycopg, PyArrow, matplotlib4.6.6 with pandas 3.1, SQLAlchemy 2.1, psycopg 3.3, PyArrow 26, matplotlib 3.11BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution, the origin of the licence of that name) 3-Clause, MIT, LGPL (GNU Lesser General Public License) 3.0, Apache 2.0The bridge from the database to analysis: Class 10 and the notebooks of Classes 11 and 12.
Valkey8.1 (Debian's package, kept current by Debian's security updates)BSD 3-ClauseKey-value: Class 11.
Apache Spark as PySpark, with OpenJDK 214.3.0 (30 October 2026)Apache 2.0; GPL (GNU General Public License) 2 with Classpath ExceptionBig data: Class 12.
Python hashlibpart of Python 3.13Python Software Foundation LicenseBlockchain: the SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) fingerprints of Class 12.
Optional demonstration engines: CouchDB, FerretDB, Neo4j Community, Cassandra, Gethcurrent container imagesApache 2.0; Apache 2.0; GPL 3.0; Apache 2.0; LGPL 3.0 and GPL 3.0Document, graph, wide-column and blockchain engines for the professor's demonstrations in Classes 11 and 12.
Optional extras: MariaDB, RDebian's packagesGPL 2.0; GPLThe other open-source relational server named in Class 4; R for Class 10.

The licences called GPL and LGPL were written by the GNU (GNU's Not Unix, the name of a free-software project) project. Every licence of the table is on the list of the Open Source Initiative, or, for SQLite, places the work in the public domain.

Your choice of toolsEvery tool in this guide is open-source software, and every one is a proposal. You may replace any of them with another suitable tool that is available to you, provided that you can justify the choice. Research your tools thoroughly: read the licence, the documentation and the date of the last release. Be creative; you may even build a tool of your own.
Good to knowMongoDB is absent on purpose: the Open Source Initiative has not approved its Server Side Public License. FerretDB, CouchDB and the JSONB type of PostgreSQL cover the document family with open-source licences.
Step 1

Run the installer

Actions 1 to 3 · 10 to 20 minutes, depending on the connection
Why this step. Installing ten tools by hand takes an afternoon and produces ten slightly different machines. The script does the same steps on every machine, records each result, and can be run again safely.

installs everything in the table above; every command in it is commented · 82 KB (kilobyte)

Open this guide in Firefox inside the VM (Virtual Machine) and download the script with the button above. It is saved to the folder Downloads.

Run it. It asks once for the password of your database user it505: 8 to 64 characters, letters, digits and . _ - + = @ %. Write the password down; DBeaver and the notebook will ask for it.

Terminal
# Go to the folder Downloads and run the installer with administrator rights.
cd ~/Downloads && sudo bash it505_setup.sh

Wait for the result table. Every line should begin with [ OK ]. If a line says [FAIL], check the internet connection and run the same command again: finished steps are skipped.

CommandWhat it installs
sudo bash it505_setup.shEverything for the three labs and the class demonstrations (the default).
sudo bash it505_setup.sh --core-onlyOnly what Labs 1 and 2 need: PostgreSQL, DBeaver, DuckDB, SQLite, JupyterLab. For a host with little memory or disk space.
sudo bash it505_setup.sh --with-demoAdds podman, the program that runs the demonstration engines in containers (professor's machine).
sudo bash it505_setup.sh --with-extrasAdds MariaDB and R.
sudo bash it505_setup.sh --pg-password NEWChanges the password of the database user it505.
sudo bash it505_setup.sh --helpLists every option.
Step of the scriptWhat it does
Basic toolsInstalls curl, git, SQLite and Python from Debian's own repositories.
PostgreSQLAdds the repository of the PostgreSQL project after checking the fingerprint of its signing key, installs version 18, creates the role it505 and the database mercadillo. If that repository cannot be reached, it installs Debian's own PostgreSQL 17 instead and says so.
Python environmentCreates a separate Python environment in /opt/it505/venv and installs JupyterLab, pandas, SQLAlchemy, psycopg, DuckDB, PyArrow and matplotlib into it.
DuckDB clientDownloads the official archive from duckdb.org and uses it only if its SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) fingerprint equals the published one.
DBeaverAdds DBeaver's package repository and installs the Community edition.
Valkey, SparkInstalls Valkey from Debian; installs OpenJDK 21 and PySpark.
Course folderCreates ~/it505 with the folders data, starter and backups, and adds the lab settings to your terminal.
Helper commandInstalls the command it505.
✔ Done when: the result table shows [ OK ] on every line.
Step 2

Prove it: the self-test

Actions 4 and 5 · 2 minutes
Why this step. An installation that reports no error is not yet proven to work. The self-test uses each tool the way a lab will use it and shows the answer.

Close the terminal and open a new one, so that the lab settings are loaded. Then run the self-test.

Terminal
# Use every tool once, the way a lab will use it, and report PASS or FAIL for each.
it505 selftest

Read the lines. Thirteen should say [PASS]. Then look at the summary of the machine.

Terminal
# Show every tool with its version and its state in one table.
it505 status
Line of the self-testWhat it provesUsed in
Flat fileThe five-row test file is in place.Class 2
File-based (two lines)SQLite answers; DuckDB reads a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) file directly from the disk.Class 2, Lab 1
Relational (two lines)The PostgreSQL server accepts the role it505 with its password; a recursive query works.Classes 4 to 10, Labs 1 and 2
DocumentPostgreSQL reads a field out of a JSONB (binary JSON, a data type of PostgreSQL) value.Class 11, Lab 3
Notebook (two lines)pandas receives a query result through SQLAlchemy; JupyterLab is installed.Class 10, Lab 2
Key-valueValkey stores a value with an expiry time and returns it.Class 11, Lab 3
Big data (two lines)DuckDB writes and reads a Parquet file; Apache Spark starts and counts rows.Class 12, Lab 3
LedgerPython computes a SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) fingerprint.Class 12, Lab 3
ClientDBeaver Community is installed.from Class 1
✔ Done when: the self-test ends with 13 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed.
Step 3

DBeaver: connect to PostgreSQL

Actions 6 to 8 · 5 minutes
Why this step. DBeaver is the window through which you will send SQL (Structured Query Language) to the databases for the rest of the course. The connection is created once and then kept.

Start DBeaver: Menu > Programming > DBeaver. Close the offer to create a sample database. Choose New connection, pick PostgreSQL, and choose Next.

Enter Host localhost, Port 5432, Database mercadillo, Username it505 and your password. Choose Test Connection; allow DBeaver to download the PostgreSQL driver (this needs the internet, once). When the test reports Connected, choose Finish.

Open an SQL editor with the button SQL, type the statement, and run it with Ctrl+Enter.

SQL
-- Ask the server for its version: the shortest statement that proves the connection.
SELECT version();
Good to knowA graphical client talks to a database server through a driver. DBeaver uses JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) drivers and downloads the one for each kind of database the first time you connect. A first connection therefore fails without the internet; later ones do not need it.
✔ Done when: the result shows one row that begins with PostgreSQL 18.
Step 4

DBeaver: a DuckDB file and a CSV file

Actions 9 and 10 · 4 minutes
Why this step. A file-based database needs no server: the whole database is one file. DuckDB can also query a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) file where it lies, which is how Class 2 opens the starter file of the labs.

Choose New connection, pick DuckDB, and choose Next. As Path enter /home/student/it505/data/mercadillo.duckdb with your own login name in place of student; choose Create, then Test Connection (the driver is downloaded once), then Finish.

Open an SQL (Structured Query Language) editor on the DuckDB connection and query the test file. Use your own login name in the path.

SQL
-- Read the test file where it lies on the disk and show all its rows.
SELECT * FROM '/home/student/it505/starter/it505_smoke_test.csv';
Good to knowThe file it505_smoke_test.csv has five invented rows and exists only for these checks. The starter dataset of the labs is handed out in class; put it into the folder ~/it505/data.
✔ Done when: the result grid shows five rows: notebook, pencil, eraser, ruler, folder.
Step 5

JupyterLab: from Python to the database

Actions 11 and 12 · 4 minutes
Why this step. Class 10 connects the database to a statistical tool. This step proves that the connection works, so that the class can spend its time on the analysis.

In a terminal start the notebook. JupyterLab opens in Firefox, in the course folder.

Terminal
# Start JupyterLab in the course folder and open it in the browser.
it505 notebook

In the file list open the folder starter, then 00_environment_check.ipynb. Click into the first code cell and press Shift+Enter; type your database password when the cell asks for it. Run the second cell the same way. To stop JupyterLab, return to the terminal and press Ctrl+C twice.

Good to knowThe notebook asks for the password every time through getpass. A password is never written into a notebook, because notebooks are shared and handed in.
✔ Done when: the first cell shows the PostgreSQL version as a one-row table; the second shows the five test rows.
Step 6

Five prompts, and where everything is

Actions 13 and 14 · 5 minutes
Why this step. Each database tool has its own text prompt and its own command to leave it. Meeting all five once saves time in every later lab.

Try each prompt once: start the tool with the command of the first column, type the line of the second column, and leave with the command of the third.

Start the toolType this lineLeave withWhat you have met
psqlSELECT current_user, current_database();\qThe terminal client of PostgreSQL, connected to the database mercadillo.
sqlite3SELECT 6 * 7;.quitSQLite, here with a database that exists only in memory.
duckdbSELECT 6 * 7 AS answer;.exitDuckDB, likewise in memory.
valkey-cliPINGexitThe client of Valkey; the server answers PONG.
pythonimport duckdb, pandas, pysparkexit()The Python of the course. No message means that the three libraries are present.

Learn the map of the machine from the table below, and look at the folder ~/it505 in the file manager.

WhatWhere
Your course folder~/it505 with data (your files), starter (test files), backups
PostgreSQLserver on localhost, port 5432; database mercadillo; user it505. In a terminal, psql alone connects to it.
Valkeyserver on localhost, port 6379; client valkey-cli
DuckDB and SQLiteno server; a database is the file you name. Keep such files in ~/it505/data.
The course Python/opt/it505/venv; in a new terminal the commands python, pip and jupyter already point to it
Start, stop a serverit505 stop postgresql, it505 start postgresql; the same with valkey
Log of the installer/var/log/it505-setup.log
Helpit505 help
✔ Done when: you have entered and left all five prompts.
Step 7

For the professor: demonstration engines

Optional · containers started on demand
Why this step. Classes 11 and 12 show a document database, a graph database, a wide-column store and a blockchain node at work. These engines are heavy; they run in containers on the professor's machine and only while they are being shown. Students do not install them.

Add podman, the program that runs containers, then list the engines.

Terminal
# Run the installer again with the option that adds podman; finished steps are skipped.
sudo bash ~/Downloads/it505_setup.sh --with-demo
Terminal
# List the demonstration engines and whether each one is running.
it505 demo list
EngineStartThen
Apache CouchDB (document)it505 demo start couchdbOpen the web interface http://localhost:5984/_utils in Firefox; user it505, password as printed.
FerretDB (document, MongoDB protocol on PostgreSQL)it505 demo start ferretdbit505 demo shell ferretdb opens its shell.
Neo4j Community (graph)it505 demo start neo4jOpen http://localhost:7474; user neo4j, password as printed.
Apache Cassandra (wide-column)it505 demo start cassandraWait about a minute, then it505 demo shell cassandra.
Geth in development mode (a private Ethereum chain, no real money)it505 demo start gethit505 demo shell geth, then for example eth.blockNumber.
Stop everythingit505 demo stop allThe data of each engine are kept until it505 demo rm NAME.
For the professorStart one engine at a time and raise the Base Memory of your VM (Virtual Machine) to 6 or 8 GB (gigabyte) first (VirtualBox Manager > Settings > System, with the VM powered off): Neo4j and Cassandra each take about 1 GB. The first start of an engine downloads its image, several hundred megabytes, so start each one once before class. Every engine listens only on localhost.
AttentionThe demonstration engines could not be started in the place where this guide was written, because no container registry was reachable there. The commands follow each project's published instructions. Rehearse each engine once before you show it.
Step 8

Back up, snapshot, export

Actions 16 to 18 · 5 minutes
Why this step. Your lab work lives in two places: the databases and the course folder. One command saves both into one file. A snapshot protects the whole machine, and an appliance file hands the finished machine to someone else.

Write a backup, then copy the file out of the VM (Virtual Machine): upload it to the course platform or your own cloud storage from Firefox inside the guest.

Terminal
# Save the databases, the course folder and the DBeaver settings into one file.
it505 backup
Terminal
# List the backup files with their sizes, to see that the new one is there.
ls -lh ~/it505/backups

Shut the guest down (Menu > Leave > Shutdown) and take the snapshot 02-toolbox-ready in VirtualBox Manager, tab Snapshots.

To bring a backup back, on this machine or on a rebuilt one: name the file.

Terminal
# Load a backup file back into the databases and the course folder; use the name of your own file.
it505 restore ~/it505/backups/it505-backup-20261121-1248.tar.gz
The backup containsIt does not contain
Every PostgreSQL database that belongs to it505; the folder ~/it505 (files up to 100 MB each); the SQL (Structured Query Language) scripts and the connection list of DBeaver.Files larger than 100 MB (megabyte), such as the ten-million-row files of Class 12, which can be produced again; the content of Valkey; the demonstration engines.
For the professorTo hand the finished machine to the class: create a neutral account first (for example student with a temporary password that you announce), shut down, then choose File > Export Appliance, select IT505-Lab, keep the format Open Virtualization Format 1.0, and choose Strip all network adapter MAC (Media Access Control) addresses. The result is one file, IT505-Lab.ova, of several gigabytes. Students import it with step 6 of Guide 1 and change the password at once.
✔ Done when: a backup file exists outside the VM, and the snapshot 02-toolbox-ready is listed.
Help

If something goes wrong

Eight frequent situations, with their cause and remedy
What you seeCause and remedy
A step of the installer says [FAIL]Almost always the network. Check that Firefox opens a web page, then run the same command again. The reason is in the last lines of /var/log/it505-setup.log.
it505: command not foundThe installer did not reach its last step, or the terminal is older than the installation. Run the installer again; open a new terminal.
psql: error: connection to server ... refusedThe PostgreSQL server is not running: it505 start postgresql, then it505 status.
password authentication failed for user "it505"Wrong password. Set a new one: sudo bash ~/Downloads/it505_setup.sh --pg-password NEW, then use it in DBeaver.
DBeaver cannot download a driverNo internet connection in the guest, or a network that blocks the download. Try another network once; the driver is then kept.
The Spark line of the self-test fails with a memory errorThe VM (Virtual Machine) has less than 3 GB (gigabyte) of memory. Give it 4096 MB (megabyte) as described in Guide 1, step 4, or skip Spark on this machine and use the cloud twin of Guide 4 for Class 12.
The disk of the guest is fulldf -h / shows the free space. Delete large files in ~/it505/data, or empty the package cache with sudo apt clean.
Everything is brokenVirtualBox Manager, tab Snapshots: restore 02-toolbox-ready, then it505 restore with your newest backup file.

Version notes

  • Every animation is a drawing made for this guide from the official documentation of each product; none is a screenshot of the product. Labels, colours and positions on your screen will differ in details.
  • Version numbers are those current on 21 November 2026. If you see a newer version, use it: the steps stay the same unless a note in the guide says otherwise.
  • PostgreSQL 19.0 appeared on 19 November 2026. The installer stays with the 18 series for this course; --pg-version 19 selects the new one.
  • The installer was run for real on Ubuntu 24.04 during its tests: basic tools, PostgreSQL (through the fallback to the distribution's package), the Python environment, DuckDB (through its fallback), Valkey, Spark, the course folder and the helper all completed, and the self-test passed 12 of 13 checks (DBeaver's site was not reachable from there). It could not be run on Debian 13, in VirtualBox, or with the PostgreSQL and DBeaver repositories reachable. Run it once on your own machine before class.
  • The screen texts in the animations show the real layout of the scripts' output with the version numbers expected on Debian 13.
